name: CPU Radix Sort for Face Centroids
definition: An out-of-place sorting algorithm used on the CPU to sort face centroids, achieving linear time complexity at the expense of auxiliary memory.
summary: CPU Radix Sort for Face Centroids is a linear-time CPU fallback for volume splatting that sorts floating-point centroids by converting them to integers and using LSD radix sort, outperforming general-purpose algorithms when viewing directions change frequently.
